subject: Capacity index & GPU onramp tasks for Q3 renewal
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Miles Gordon <miles.gordon@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity index & GPU onramp tasks for Q3 renewal

Miles —

Congrats on the progress this quarter. As we head into the renewal conversation for Q3 capacity, I want to propose a small operational exercise that will make the capacity ask more defensible and reduce friction when you need short-term bursts. We call it a "capacity index": a concise mapping from observed throughput (tokens/sec and concurrent sessions) to committed GPU slots plus an onramp trigger.

Quick ask: can you share a representative 24‑hour sample (UTC) of production traffic for a recent peak day? A CSV with timestamp, rolling concurrency, avg tokens/sec, and 90th latency is perfect. I attached our capacity-index-template to speed this up.

What we'll deliver after that sample:
- an index showing breakpoints (steady state, pre-surge, surge) and suggested committed GPU equivalence
- a recommended onramp checklist (operational steps + expected time to provision)
- suggested tranche sizes for a conservative top-up and an accelerated top-up, with cost delta estimates

If that sounds good, I'll schedule a 30‑minute working session this week to walk through the template and get alignment on the onramp SLAs.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
Attachments: capacity-index-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Miles Gordon <miles.gordon@atlashealth.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity index & GPU onramp tasks for Q3 renewal

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the pragmatic approach. We can pull that 24‑hour sample; attaching a trimmed export (usage-sample-202704.csv) and a short note on our traffic patterns:
- Typical steady concurrency: 120–150 sessions
- Burst windows: 2x–4x lasting 12–40 minutes, usually driven by scheduled data ingestion jobs plus occasional marketing-driven spikes
- Models: mixture of Llama-2-70b (quantized) and a small custom 13B that we hot-swap for cost reasons

Two asks from our side: 1) keep the onramp conservative (we've seen over-provisioning blow budgets), and 2) include a "warm KV cache" step so model swap cold starts don't kill latency.

I'll be available Tuesday morning if you want to walk through the CSV live.

—Miles
Director of Platform, Atlas Health
Attachments: usage-sample-202704.csv (CSV)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity index & GPU onramp tasks for Q3 renewal

Looping in a quick internal ops checklist and proposed MAP (mutual action plan) for the working session:

Action items before the call:
- Hannah: confirm sample received and share pre-read (that's done).
- Ben: run the capacity-index-template against Miles' CSV and push a draft index to the shared drive (I'll do an initial pass tonight).
- Karthik: prepare tranche sizing options (conservative, standard, aggressive) with hourly cost deltas and expected latency SLO impact.

On the call we'll:
1) validate breakpoint logic (concurrency -> GPU equivalence)
2) agree operational onramp SLA (time-to-provision, warm-cache steps, rollback)
3) pick a commit/top-up recommendation for the renewal (commit + flexible buffer or commit + burst pool)

Attached a short onramp-checklist.pdf that mirrors our standard operational playbook — please review and highlight anything Atlas specifically requires.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: onramp-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity index & GPU onramp tasks for Q3 renewal

Quick modeling note after a first pass on the CSV:
- If we map 150 steady sessions to 12 x A100-equivalent slots (quantized Llama-2-70b), a 3x burst (450 sessions) maps to ~36 slots.
- Recommend a conservative onramp tranche of +8 slots (warm-cache enabled) as a first incremental commit; an aggressive tranche of +24 for customers who need sub-200ms P95 during spikes.
- Cost delta (monthly): +8 slots ≈ $18k, +24 slots ≈ $50k (estimates include KV warm-cache preload time and short-lived burst instances).

I also recommend adding an automatic pre-warm trigger at 80% of steady concurrency sustained for 3 minutes — reduces cold start tail latency.

Karthik
Principal Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
